mechanism.basis: Two catalog records state mechanisms that point in opposite directions, so no direction is used.
disagreements: The catalog records different mechanisms for WAS: Wiskott–Aldrich syndrome (WAS LOF) (loss of function), X-linked neutropenia/myelodysplasia (gain of function). Ask for one disease to get a direction.
The variant's mechanism candidates (stability) would fit a protein that does too little, but a residue candidate does not state which way the activity moves, so the direction stays unknown.

action_rule_table.why: The protein does too much, so a molecule can only help by reducing what it does.
The protein does something it should not do, so a molecule can only help by removing that activity.
The protein does too little, so a molecule can only help by bringing the activity back.
One working copy makes too little protein, so a molecule can only help by bringing the activity back.
The broken copy blocks the working copy, so a molecule can only help by clearing the broken copy or by working around it.
No record states which way this protein's activity moves, so no required action is derived and nothing is ruled out on direction.

ranking_rule: The direction check first: a molecule whose action matches the mechanism comes before one whose direction could not be checked.

Then how directly the bridge connects: this very protein, then a protein up or down the pathway, then a protein this one binds, then a protein with a similar pocket, then another disease with the same mechanism.
Then the strongest kind of record in the chain: experimental, then clinical database, then curated database, then published literature, then computational prediction.
Then whether the record is on this protein alone rather than on a group of related proteins.
Then the highest clinical phase recorded for the molecule, because a molecule given to people has clinical records behind it.
Then the measured activity against the protein, as the strength of that record.
Then the number of different sources in the chain.
There is no combined score, no probability of success and no claim that a molecule would work.
limits: No record states which way this protein's activity moves, so nothing was ruled out on direction and every candidate is labelled unknown.
Every row is a hypothesis Helix built from records. None of it is a treatment, a dose or advice.
A candidate says a molecule acts in the direction this mechanism needs. It does not say the molecule would work.
Tissue and cell type were not checked, so a protein may not be present where it matters.
Only molecules that ChEMBL records a mechanism for are considered. A molecule without such a record is missing from both lists.
A molecule in the ruled-out list is ruled out for this mechanism. It may be right for another disease of the same gene.
The catalog lists 2 diseases for WAS. Ask for one of them to get a mechanism and a direction for that disease.
